transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-06-04
Start: 14:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jonah Kim (Redwood SE), Alex Rivera (Blueleaf Eng Mgr), Priya Shah (Blueleaf Search Eng), Tom Nguyen (Blueleaf CTO - joined ~00:20)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Quick hosted API walkthrough focusing on embeddings + reranking for improving search relevance. SE demoed vector embeddings endpoint, similarity search demo using Redwood-hosted vectors + simple rerank endpoint to boost doc relevance. Discussed latency vs cost tradeoffs, VPC/private options, security concerns (SOC2, KMS), and pilot next steps. Action: send pricing + SOW, share benchmark scripts, Blueleaf to provide sample logs.

Topics: Hosted embeddings endpoint, reranking endpoint (cross-encoder), Redwood Console search metrics, batching & caching, pilot scope and success criteria, security/compliance questions.

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE on this one, with Jonah our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:00:12] Alex: Good thanks, Alex here. Excited to see the walkthrough. We've been looking at ways to improve our search relevancy for product docs and knowledge base.
[00:00:22] Priya: Hi all, Priya - I handle search infra, mostly Elastic today. We're curious about embeddings-based rerank flows.
[00:00:30] Jonah: Awesome, quick agenda — 1) show embeddings endpoint and how to index vectors, 2) demo a simple nearest-neighbor search + rerank using Redwood's hosted API, 3) show Console metrics and Optimize suggestions, 4) Q&A and next steps. Sound good?
[00:00:42] Alex: Yep.
[00:00:45] Jonah: Great, i'm going to share my screen. Apologies if the auto-transcription calls the product Red wood or something, the audio sometimes does that.
[00:00:58] [screen share starts] Jonah: So here's the Console, this is our hosted-api region in us-west-2. First call: embeddings create endpoint. We'll hit /v1/embeddings with a batch of docs. Note — we support 1024 and 768 dims depending on model family, and we provide metadata with each vector.
[00:01:20] Priya: Wait, which model are you using for the demo?
[00:01:24] Jonah: Good call — for this demo i'm using our open-family rwd-embedding-1 (demo config) which is 1024-d. In production you'd pick from the catalog; we also provide Redwood-verified perf profiles.
[00:01:34] [00:01:34] Alex: How long does embedding inference take? Latency matters for our real-time features.
[00:01:38] Jonah: For a single-tile call — small text — median ~22ms per embedding on hosted. For batch of 128 it's amortized — you see better throughput, but we expose the batch size control. That's the tradeoff: lower token latency for single calls vs lower cost per embed for batching.
[00:01:55] Maya: Also note that for search we often do asynchronous indexing — compute embeddings in background and write to vector DB or Redwood's managed vector store.
[00:02:05] Priya: Do you host the vectors or do we need Pinecone/Elastic?
[00:02:09] Jonah: You can do either. For speed of pilot, many customers use Redwood's hosted vector indexing (managed store) — it's simpler, low ops. If you already have a vector DB like Pinecone/Weaviate or use Elastic + vec extension, you can keep it. Rerank stage can be done server-side via our rerank endpoint so you don't have to move all traffic.
[00:02:26] [00:02:26] Alex: Show the rerank flow please.
[00:02:29] Jonah: Sure — here's a typical pipeline: 1) user query -> embeddings similarity search -> top N candidates -> call rerank endpoint (cross-encoder) with query + candidates -> return reordered list. I'll run a quick example against the sample KB.
[00:02:45] [00:02:45] Jonah: (typing) Ok running similarity search, returning top 8. Now call rerank /v1/rerank with query + 8 docs. Rerank returns scores and explanation tokens (we can surface explainability metadata).
[00:03:05] Priya: What's the latency on rerank? That seems heavier.
[00:03:08] Jonah: For a cross-encoder rerank of 8 candidates median ~120-170ms on hosted depending on model size. We expose smaller, faster re-rank models if you need sub-100ms. Also our Optimize recommendations can suggest using a lightweight hybrid: use embed nearest neighbors for recall and a small cross-encoder for top re-rank.
[00:03:28] Alex: If we do this for product search at scale, do we need Dedicated?
[00:03:32] Maya: Depends on throughput & SLAs. Most customers start hosted to validate relevance improvements; if you need predictable latency at high QPS or data isolation, Redwood Dedicated or Private are options. We can size a Dedicated pool based on your throughput.
[00:03:45] [00:03:45] Tom (joined): Sorry I'm late — CTO here. Quick Q: encryption of vectors at rest and KMS support?
[00:03:53] Jonah: Yes — hosted vectors at rest can be encrypted, and for Private/Dedicated we support customer-managed KMS/HSM. We also have audit logs and RBAC via SSO (SAML/OAuth).
[00:04:06] Tom: SOC2?
[00:04:08] Maya: SOC2 Type II report available, we can share the security pack after the call.
[00:04:15] [00:04:15] Jonah: Back to the demo — here's Console trace for the query I just ran. You can see token-level breakdown and cost estimate per request. Under Optimize, we have recommendations: e.g., switch to 512-d model, enable prefix cache for frequent queries, or add small batch precomputations.
[00:04:36] Priya: Can you show an example where rerank improves a bad recall case?
[00:04:40] Jonah: Yup — here I have a sample query 'how to reset SSO session' — initial NN results include a config doc and a user guide; after rerank the SSO troubleshooting doc moves to top because cross-encoder captures the query intent better. I'll play both outputs.
[00:04:58] [00:04:58] Jonah: (reads) Pre-rerank top result: 'SSO config overview' — not ideal. Post-rerank top result: 'SSO session reset troubleshooting' — that's what we want.
[00:05:12] Alex: Nice — that matches what we see in offline evals. What metrics should we track during a pilot?
[00:05:18] Maya: Usually precision@k, MRR (mean reciprocal rank), time-to-first-byte, and cost per query. Also false positive rate for sensitive docs if you have privacy constraints.
[00:05:28] [00:05:28] Priya: Regarding cost, do you have ballpark numbers? We currently budgeted $X per month for Elastic + custom ranking infra.
[00:05:35] Jonah: Ballpark — hosted embeddings are billed per 1k embeddings; rerank billed per request (model-dependent). For many customers, the increase in relevance allows tuning down the number of candidates and overall token usage, so net cost can be similar or lower. We'll send exact pricing for your expected QPS.
[00:05:52] Alex: Any limits on payload size or metadata fields on vectors?
[00:05:57] Jonah: We support metadata up to a reasonable payload (we'll share the spec). You can store doc IDs, routing keys, etc. Also support TTL on vectors if you want ephemeral indexes.
[00:06:10] [00:06:10] Maya: Quick note on fallback policies — Console lets you configure automatic fallback to cheaper model variants or to cached responses if latency SLOs are missed.
[00:06:22] Priya: How about A/B testing for a rollout?
[00:06:25] Jonah: We have canary rollouts and traffic splits in Console. You can measure success against your eval set and Gradually shift traffic.
[00:06:36] [00:06:36] Alex: Ok, curious about benchmark. Can you run our sample queries and show the delta?
[00:06:41] Jonah: Yes — for the pilot we'll run a benchmark with your 10k sample queries. We'll generate embeddings, index the vectors, run NN + rerank and compute MRR/P@1. I'll provide the scripts — they're in the repo I linked in chat.
[00:06:57] [00:06:57] Priya: Chat link's showing a repo called 'redwood-search-playbook' — right?
[00:07:01] Jonah: Yep, that's it. Contains the benchmark scripts, instructions for running locally vs using hosted endpoints, and sample expected outputs.
[00:07:10] Alex: A couple security follow-ups — can we ensure logs exclude PII and how long do you retain logs by default?
[00:07:16] Jonah: Default retention is 30 days for verbose traces, but enterprise customers can request longer or shorter retention and have audit-only exports. Logs can be redacted or filtered — we'll share the security doc with specifics.
[00:07:30] [00:07:30] Tom: For an enterprise contract, can we bring Redwood under our master agreement?
[00:07:33] Maya: Absolutely — once we scope Dedicated or Private we can work with legal. We'll attach standard terms to the SOW and coordinate with your procurement.
[00:07:44] Priya: One more product question — do you have offline rerank training or is rerank purely inference?
[00:07:49] Jonah: Right now the rerank endpoint is inference-only (cross-encoder scoring). For learned rankers, many customers combine Redwood inference with their offline training pipelines and then host a small model for rerank. We also support storing human-labeled eval sets in Console for regression monitoring.
[00:08:05] [00:08:05] Jonah: I'm going to demo Console's optimize tab briefly — here it flags a prompt set where rerank causes latency >200ms and suggests a smaller rerank model or reduce candidate N from 16 to 6. You can accept the recommendation or run a simulation.
[00:08:23] Alex: That simulation feature sounds useful so we can measure quality-cost tradeoffs without impacting prod.
[00:08:28] Jonah: Exactly.
[00:08:31] [00:08:31] Maya: Ok wrapping toward next steps — we'll send pricing + SOW, Jonah will share benchmark scripts + instructions, and Blueleaf to upload sample query logs to the shared S3. We'll aim to run the pilot next week.
[00:08:45] Alex: Sounds good.
[00:08:47] Tom: Agree. Please send security pack.
[00:08:51] Maya: Will do — SOC2, penetration test summary, network diagrams, KMS docs.
[00:08:58] Priya: Quick note — can we test both hosted vector store and a flow where we keep vectors in our Pinecone? We want to compare.
[00:09:05] Jonah: Yep we'll include both in the benchmark. We'll provide scripts for pushing vectors to Pinecone and an alternative for Redwood-managed store.
[00:09:14] [00:09:14] Maya: Any other questions?
[00:09:18] Alex: None from me. Thanks for the demo.
[00:09:21] Priya: Thanks.
[00:09:23] Maya: Thanks everyone — recap in chat and I'll follow up with SOW and security docs.

Meeting end: 14:48 PT

Recap / Final notes (auto):
- Pilot scope: 10k queries benchmark, compare hosted vector-store vs Pinecone, measure MRR/P@1 and latency, iterate on rerank model size.
- Security: Redwood to share SOC2 and KMS docs.
- Pricing: Maya to send tailored pricing + monthly pilot estimate.

Links shared in chat: redwood-search-playbook (benchmark scripts), security-pack link (to be attached in follow-up), pricing template (internal).
